subject: Economy
sub_topic: India's rank in major global indices

concepts.name: Global Hunger Index (GHI): Methodology, Criticism and India's Response
key_dimensions: Four indicators used: undernourishment, child wasting, child stunting, child mortality — and their weightage
Published by Concern Worldwide and Welthungerhilfe (NOT a UN body — common trap)
India's consistent objection to methodology, especially reliance on opinion polls for undernourishment data
Distinction between GHI and FAO's State of Food Security Report — different agencies, different findings

concepts.name: Human Development Index (HDI): Components, Formula and India's Trajectory
key_dimensions: Three dimensions: long and healthy life, knowledge, decent standard of living — measured via GNI per capita (PPP), not GDP
UNDP publishes via Human Development Report — distinction from HDR's thematic focus each year
Gender Development Index (GDI) vs Gender Inequality Index (GII) — overlap trap: both are HDR products but measure different things
India's rank stagnation despite economic growth — reason: GNI per capita drag and education indicators

concepts.name: Global Innovation Index (GII): Publisher, Parameters and India's Rise
key_dimensions: Published by WIPO (not WEF — common confusion) in partnership with INSEAD and Cornell University
Two sub-indices: Innovation Input and Innovation Output — India's unique strength in Output efficiency ratio
India's rank improvement from 81 (2015) to top 40 — used as policy achievement by GOI
Parameters: Institutions, Human capital & research, Infrastructure, Market sophistication, Business sophistication, Knowledge outputs, Creative outputs

concepts.name: Ease of Doing Business (EoDB) Index: Methodology Change and India's Performance
key_dimensions: Published by World Bank — DISCONTINUED in 2021 after data manipulation controversy (Doing Business 2018 & 2020 reports)
India's rise from rank 142 (2014) to 63 (2020) — often cited in governance reforms context
Replacement framework: Business Ready (B-READY) index — its new pillars differ from original 10 parameters
UPSC trap: Questions may still reference old parameters (Starting a business, Paying taxes, Enforcing contracts, etc.) as historical data

concepts.name: Global Competitiveness Index (GCI): WEF Framework and Pillar Structure
key_dimensions: Published by World Economic Forum (WEF) — NOT World Bank
12 pillars grouped into 3 sub-indices: Basic requirements, Efficiency enhancers, Innovation & sophistication
GCI 4.0 (2018 revision) added 'Agility' factors — distinction from older GCI methodology
India's rank fluctuation and specific weak pillars: health, labour market efficiency, financial market development

concepts.name: Press Freedom Index: Publisher, Criteria and India's Controversial Ranking
key_dimensions: Published by Reporters Without Borders (RSF) — a French NGO, NOT a UN or intergovernmental body
Five criteria: political context, legal framework, economic context, sociocultural context, safety
India's low rank (150s range) vs government's rebuttal about methodology subjectivity
Distinction from Freedom of the Press report by Freedom House — two different indices on same theme

concepts.name: Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI): Methodology Trap and Publisher
key_dimensions: Published by Transparency International (TI) — NOT a government or UN body
Based on perception of corruption in public sector only — does NOT measure private sector or actual corruption levels
Composite index drawn from 13 different surveys/assessments — secondary data based
Score vs Rank distinction: India's score improvement may not reflect rank improvement if other countries improve more

concepts.name: World Happiness Report: Index vs Report and Measurement Parameters
key_dimensions: Published by UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN) — NOT UNDP
Based on Gallup World Poll — self-reported life evaluation (Cantril ladder), NOT objective metrics
Six variables: GDP per capita, social support, healthy life expectancy, freedom, generosity, perceptions of corruption
India consistently ranks in lower half — contrast with high GDP growth narrative; UPSC uses this for prelim traps

concepts.name: Environmental Performance Index (EPI): Publisher, India's Rank and Controversy
key_dimensions: Published by Yale and Columbia Universities — NOT UNEP (common confusion)
India ranked last (180th) in 2022 — government strongly rejected methodology, especially air quality weighting
32 performance indicators across 11 issue categories under two objectives: Ecosystem Vitality and Environmental Health
Distinction from UNEP's Global Environment Outlook — different product, different publisher

concepts.name: Global Gender Gap Index (GGGI): WEF Framework vs Gender Inequality Index (GII)
key_dimensions: Published by WEF — four sub-indices: Economic participation, Educational attainment, Health and survival, Political empowerment
Measures gap (parity), NOT absolute levels — a country can score well on education parity even with low absolute levels
India's lowest score on Economic participation and Health sub-indices — specific weak areas
UPSC trap: GGGI (WEF) vs GII (UNDP/HDR) — different publishers, different parameters, often confused

concepts.name: Logistics Performance Index (LPI): World Bank Framework and PM GatiShakti Connection
key_dimensions: Published by World Bank — six components: Customs, Infrastructure, International shipments, Logistics competence, Tracking & tracing, Timeliness
India's rank improvement linked to policy reforms: Dedicated Freight Corridors, ULIP, PM GatiShakti
Biennial publication — important for understanding frequency of data (not annual)
Distinction from National Logistics Policy (2022) targets which use LPI as benchmark

concepts.name: Financial Secrecy Index and Basel AML Index: Anti-Money Laundering Frameworks
key_dimensions: Financial Secrecy Index: Published by Tax Justice Network — measures offshore financial secrecy, NOT corruption
Basel AML Index: Published by Basel Institute on Governance — measures money laundering/terrorist financing risk
UPSC trap: Both deal with illicit finance but measure opposite things — secrecy provision vs risk exposure
India's FATF membership and mutual evaluation reports — connection to AML compliance rankings

concepts.name: Global Firepower Index and Military Strength Rankings: Limitations and Parameters
key_dimensions: Published by GlobalFirepower.com — a private entity, NOT an official intergovernmental body
PowerIndex score considers 60+ factors including manpower, equipment, finances, geography, logistics
Nuclear capability is NOT directly factored in — acknowledged limitation
India consistently ranks 4th globally — used in Prelims but source credibility is a GS essay angle

concepts.name: World Press Freedom Index vs Democracy Index: Two Separate Frameworks
key_dimensions: Democracy Index: Published by Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU) — five categories including Flawed Democracy (India's classification)
Four regime types: Full democracy, Flawed democracy, Hybrid regime, Authoritarian regime
India classified as 'Flawed Democracy' — specific reasons: civil liberties concerns, functioning of government score
UPSC trap: EIU Democracy Index ≠ Freedom House's Freedom in the World report — different publishers, different classifications

concepts.name: India's Rank in Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) Index: SDSN Framework
key_dimensions: Published by SDSN and Bertelsmann Stiftung — NOT UN officially, though aligned with UN agenda
India's weakest SDGs: SDG 2 (Zero Hunger), SDG 3 (Good Health), SDG 15 (Life on Land)
Distinction between SDG Index and Voluntary National Reviews (VNRs) submitted to HLPF — different mechanisms
NITI Aayog's SDG India Index — domestic index for state-level tracking, different from global SDG Index

concepts.name: World Intellectual Property Indicators and Patent Filing Rankings
key_dimensions: Published by WIPO — distinct from GII (also WIPO) — covers patents, trademarks, industrial designs
India's rise as top patent filing country — distinction between resident vs non-resident filings
PCT (Patent Cooperation Treaty) applications vs domestic filings — India's rank differs across categories
Connection to National IPR Policy 2016 and 'Creative India, Innovative India' framework

concepts.name: Fragile States Index (FSI): Publisher, Indicators and India's Position
key_dimensions: Published by Fund for Peace (FFP) — a US-based NGO, NOT a UN body
12 indicators across Cohesion, Economic, Political and Social categories — UPSC tests specific indicator names
India classified in 'Elevated Warning' category — distinction from 'Alert' (most fragile) and 'Sustainable' categories
Formerly called Failed States Index — name change in 2014 is a potential trap question

concepts.name: Energy Transition Index (ETI) and India's Renewable Energy Rankings
key_dimensions: ETI published by WEF — measures progress on energy transition across equity, security and sustainability
Distinction from International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA) reports and REN21 Global Status Report
India's rank in installed renewable capacity (globally top 4) vs per capita consumption — narrative gap
UPSC trap: Multiple agencies publish energy reports — WEF (ETI), IEA (World Energy Outlook), IRENA, REN21 — different focus areas

concepts.name: Networked Readiness Index (NRI) and Digital Competitiveness: Publisher Distinction
key_dimensions: NRI published by Portulans Institute — NOT WEF (WEF used to publish it till 2016, now discontinued by them)
Four pillars: Technology, People, Governance, Impact — with sub-pillars
IMD World Digital Competitiveness Ranking — separate index by IMD Business School, Lausanne
UPSC trap: Digital India achievements cited against NRI vs IMD rankings — different methodologies yield different results

concepts.name: Global TB Report and India's Disease Burden Rankings: WHO Framework
key_dimensions: Published annually by WHO — India accounts for largest share of global TB burden (~26%)
India's National Strategic Plan and 'TB-Mukt Bharat' — target of TB elimination by 2025 vs global target of 2030
Distinction between incidence rate, prevalence rate and mortality rate — UPSC tests definitional precision
Global Fund to Fight AIDS, TB and Malaria — financing mechanism distinct from WHO's reporting function
